sessions.phase_label: Separate TPEC proposal pre-engagement and scoping
Agua Arc RFQ scope negotiation and kickoff
Draft review, revisions, and final delivery

requirements.title: Full-Document Layout and Graphic Treatment
requirements.definition: Create a cohesive, clear, and professionally organized layout and graphic treatment across the complete Agua Arc RFQ response.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the overall visual layout system only; branding, typography, photos, structured content, and output formats are independently testable Requirements.

requirements.title: Agua Arc Branding
requirements.definition: Use Agua Arc's identity, including its logo and brand colors, rather than GreenLatinos branding in the proposal design.
requirements.boundary_note: Brand identity can change independently of the document's general layout and is therefore separate from full-document graphic treatment.

requirements.title: Typography Consistency
requirements.definition: Use uniform typefaces and correct, consistent font sizes in the relevant proposal sections.
requirements.boundary_note: Typography consistency has its own acceptance criterion and can be corrected without changing branding, photographs, or structural content.

requirements.title: Required Photo Inclusion and Placement
requirements.definition: Include the client-designated proposal photos and apply later client decisions concerning their placement, relocation, removal, or substitution.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers which photos appear and where they are placed; crop-specific tree visibility is separately testable and excluded.

requirements.title: Tree Visibility in Photo Crops
requirements.definition: Crop designated proposal photographs so the requested trees remain sufficiently visible.
requirements.boundary_note: The repeated tree-visibility adjustments have a distinct modification and fix trajectory from general photo selection and placement.

requirements.title: Key-Page Background Style
requirements.definition: Use an approved background treatment for the cover, table of contents, appendix divider, and final page, replacing the disliked cream or pink wash with white or another acceptable approach.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a targeted styling obligation for a defined page set and can be modified independently of the overall layout system.

requirements.title: Fixed RFQ Section Sequence
requirements.definition: Preserve the section order established by the client's RFQ question-and-answer guidance and shown in the supplied document skeleton.
requirements.boundary_note: Section ordering is an externally constrained structural rule, distinct from visual layout and content completeness.

requirements.title: RFQ Page-Limit Compliance
requirements.definition: Format and space the proposal so it fits as closely as required within the applicable RFQ page limit.
requirements.boundary_note: Page-limit compliance can fail or be revised independently of visual quality and content inclusion; the exact authoritative numeric cap is not explicit in the supplied messages.

requirements.title: Required Section and Subsection Content
requirements.definition: Include all required narrative sections and subsections supplied for the final RFQ response.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers presence of required narrative content; tables, biographies, the organization chart, and sequence constraints have separate acceptance criteria.

requirements.title: Proposal Table Integration
requirements.definition: Incorporate the supplied proposal tables, including the budget and payment or milestone materials, and apply later replacements and row additions.
requirements.boundary_note: Individual table replacements and row changes are attributes of one table-integration mechanism rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Team Biography Integration
requirements.definition: Provide space for and incorporate the additional team biographies in the Message Agency appendix.
requirements.boundary_note: Biography placeholders and direct biography insertion form one independently changing appendix-content mechanism.

requirements.title: Organization Chart Integration
requirements.definition: Create or incorporate the organization chart into the final RFQ document layout.
requirements.boundary_note: The organization chart is an independently requested structured visual component and is not merged into the broader table or biography Requirements.

requirements.title: One-Page Proposal Letter Layout
requirements.definition: Format the opening proposal letter as a single page while allowing insertion of the client's signature and relocating displaced photographs when necessary.
requirements.boundary_note: The one-page letter has a page-specific acceptance criterion independent of the overall document page limit.

requirements.title: Proposal Table of Contents
requirements.definition: Provide and maintain a table of contents aligned with the proposal's final structure.
requirements.boundary_note: The table of contents can be revised independently when document structure changes and is therefore separate from general layout.

requirements.title: Editable Canva Source Deliverable
requirements.definition: Deliver an editable Canva design owned and accessible by the client without requiring a paid Canva subscription, using assets that remain available to free users.
requirements.boundary_note: Combines editing access, ownership, and free-asset compatibility as attributes of one Canva source-delivery mechanism; it is distinct from a reusable modular template.

requirements.title: Print-Ready PDF Deliverable
requirements.definition: Deliver the completed RFQ response as a print-ready PDF.
requirements.boundary_note: Print readiness is an output property independent of editability, hyperlink operation, and email file-size suitability.

requirements.title: Emailable PDF Deliverable
requirements.definition: Export the final response as one clean, compressed PDF whose file size supports email transmission.
requirements.boundary_note: Email suitability has a distinct file-export and file-size acceptance criterion, separate from print readiness and hyperlink correctness.

requirements.title: Functional Proposal Hyperlinks
requirements.definition: Preserve the functionality of all proposal hyperlinks through Canva editing and final PDF export.
requirements.boundary_note: Hyperlink functionality has its own executed success criterion and can fail even when the PDF exports and emails successfully.

requirements.title: Modular Reusable Proposal Template
requirements.definition: Provide a reusable proposal-template system with swappable narrative sections, resizable budget tables, and a replaceable prepared-for client line for future proposals.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently requested reusable system rather than an attribute of the one-time editable Canva file; the client later defers it to a future project.

unresolved_candidates.description: Page-limit compliance is clearly requested, but the authoritative numeric page cap cannot be established safely from the supplied messages.
The freelancer could not determine whether Section 6 Prioritization remained required; no clear resolution appears in the supplied history.
Uniform typography is required, but the intended in-text bolding rules remain unresolved because the source document used ambiguous highlighting and red text.

source_message.text: Unfortunately, that exceeds my budget and seems broader in scope than I need. Could we develop a more straightforward option? source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Good morning!

That approach works for me. Thank you.

If any other portions feel awkward, I can try trimming the content further when I review it, if that would help.

Thank you for collaborating with me on this and continuing to share progress updates.

value_updates.page_layout_strategy: use consistent page layouts with fewer section-specific custom treatments

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

I’ve attached the proposal’s first draft. The Canva link is here: [URL_006]

Here are several notes for your review:

\- **General design:** Because the document became nearly twice its initial length and the timeline was short, I prioritized a cohesive design system instead of creating many distinct layouts. This should make the revisions more manageable as well.

\- **Graphics & photos:** I placed the images in organic-shaped frames and included a handful of understated graphic elements that seemed appropriate for the overall theme without distracting from the content.

\- **Section 6: Prioritization:** I didn’t find this section in the revised tables document, so I wasn’t certain whether it was still supposed to appear in the proposal.

\- **In-text bolding:** I wasn’t fully clear on which text was meant to be bold. Some content in the Google Doc was highlighted, while other text appeared in red, and during layout I couldn’t determine which formatting was deliberate and which was editorial markup.

\- **Links:** I checked every hyperlink, and they all seem to function. However, it would be helpful to have a second reviewer test each one too.

\- **Final review:** Given the very quick turnaround, I plan to make another pass tomorrow with fresh eyes to identify anything I might have overlooked. I still wanted to deliver this to you today.

I’m looking forward to your feedback. Hopefully, the draft is in a strong place, and after your review I can fine-tune whatever you’d like changed.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer delivered the first proposal draft and reports applying a cohesive design system across the document rather than many distinct layouts.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Thank you for providing the $1400.00 estimate. That works for me.

A few items:

1) My subcontractors won’t send me their content until EOD next Wednesday, so your working period will be compressed. Would you be able to turn it around within 48-hour of receiving the final narrative content from me, followed by a 24-hour turnaround on your end for the final revisions?

2) For the branding, I’ve shifted the focus from the client’s brand to the bidder’s brand—mine! I’d like the design to reflect my company, Agua Arc. I can provide my logo and colors.

3) Because this will be the first proposal I’m submitting as a prime, and I launched my company less than a year ago and work solo, I’d like to use this proposal as a template going forward. Ideally, the template you build would have modular/swappable sections so future proposals don’t need to be recreated from the beginning. In particular, I’m imagining a) a flexible narrative-section framework, since some proposals may have 5 sections v 8 sections, b) a modular table design that can be resized for different budget structures, and c) a “prepared for \_\_\_ \[client name\]” credit line instead of client branding.

4) Regarding Canva, can I own the files without having a paid subscription? Would there be any other source files, or would everything exist solely in Canva?

Thank you!

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: 3) One additional note: please ensure the fonts are uniform, using the same typefaces in the relevant sections and the correct sizes.

value_updates.typeface_rule: use the same typefaces in relevant sections
